title: They Scored 349. It Wasn't Enough. Rain and DLS Handed Afghanistan A a Stunning Win in Dambulla.
excerpt: Prabhsimran Singh's 84, fifties from Gaikwad and Varma, and a Sooryavanshi blitz all went in vain as Afghanistan A chased down a revised target with ease in the Tri-Nation A Series.
body:
India's young guns piled up a mountain of runs. Rain washed it away.

In one of the most gut-wrenching results of the ongoing Tri-Nation A Series in Sri Lanka, Afghanistan A defeated India A by four runs via the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium on Wednesday, despite India posting a commanding 349 for 9 in 49 overs.

It was a day that began with promise and ended in frustration for Tilak Varma's side. After winning their opening match against Sri Lanka A, India A now sit at 1-1 in the tournament, their series-long momentum disrupted by a combination of Dambulla's fickle weather and an Afghan batting lineup that refused to blink.

## Three Fifties, One Giant Total, No Result

India's batting card read like a highlights reel. Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, continuing his remarkable 2026, opened the innings with characteristic aggression — smashing nine fours in a 22-ball cameo of 44 that immediately put Afghanistan's bowlers on the back foot. Not a single six, all timing, all placement. It was the kind of knock that underlines why selectors are keeping a very close eye on the teenager.

Wicketkeeper Prabhsimran Singh then took over, striking 84 off 69 balls in a display of controlled power that anchored the innings through the middle overs. He added a crucial partnership with Ruturaj Gaikwad, who compiled a steady 66 off 80 deliveries. Captain Tilak Varma matched Gaikwad's contribution with 66 of his own, ensuring India A's total crossed 300 with overs to spare.

Afghanistan medium-pacer Abdullah Ahmadzai was the lone bright spot with the ball for his side, returning figures of 5 for 68 — a five-wicket haul that would have been more celebrated had it come in a losing cause.

## Rain Rewrites the Script

With 349 on the board, India A would have fancied their chances of wrapping up a comfortable win. But the Dambulla weather had other plans. Heavy rain interrupted the second innings, and the DLS method revised Afghanistan's target to 294 from 38 overs — a stiff ask, but significantly more achievable than chasing 350 in 49.

What followed exposed India A's bowling limitations. Afghan captain Imran Mir was masterful in his run-chase, remaining unbeaten on 75 off 70 deliveries. Hassan Eisakhil set the tone with a brisk 35 off 29 balls at the top before Mir and Bahir Shah forged an unbroken century partnership that swung the match decisively.

Shah, who finished with an unbeaten 51 off 52 balls, provided the steady hand while Mir played the aggressor. India's bowlers, particularly left-arm seamer Arshad Khan, were wayward and leaked boundaries on the damp surface. The spinners — Anukul Roy and Vipraj Nigam — found no purchase, and the required rate stayed within Afghanistan's comfort zone throughout.

When persistent rain returned and the match was called off at 177 for 2 in 25.5 overs, Afghanistan A were comfortably ahead of the DLS par score.

## What It Means for the Selectors

The result carries significance beyond the tri-series standings. Several players in this India A squad are audition-pieces for the senior ODI side. Gaikwad, who is set to join the full Indian squad for the Afghanistan bilateral series as Virat Kohli's replacement, showed the composure required at the highest level. Sooryavanshi continues to build an irrefutable case for elevation.

But the bowling unit's inability to defend 349 — even accounting for DLS intervention — will concern the selectors. If India A's pace and spin attack cannot apply pressure in helpful conditions, the bench strength behind the senior bowling group looks thinner than the batting pipeline suggests.

India A next face Sri Lanka A, with a win required to keep their campaign on track. For Afghanistan A, this victory validates a squad brimming with fearless young talent, led by a captain in Imran Mir who appears destined for bigger stages.
